questions.question: Two circles of radius 7 units each, intersect in such a way that the common chord is of length 7 units. What is the common area in square units of the intersection?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of each circle = 7 units

Length of the common chord = 7 units

**Formula Used:**

Area of intersection of two circles = 2×(Area of sector - Area of triangle)

Area of sector = (θ/360) × πr²

Area of equilateral triangle = √3/4 × side²

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a964e5481925f7ef4835ce6229868f12991db8b3521f3357e1dcf6b500dce4a0.png] 

In the ΔAOB, 

All sides are equal, so it is an equilateral triangle.

i.e. θ = ∠AOB = 60° 

Now,

Area of intersection of two circles = 2×(Area of sector - Area of triangle)

⇒ Area = 2 [(θ/360) × πr2 - √3/4 × side2]

⇒ Area = 2 [(60/360) × π × 7² - √3/4 × 72]

⇒ Area = 2 × 7² [(1/6) × π - √3/4]

⇒ Area = 2 × 49 [π/6 - √3/4]

⇒ Area = 98 [π/6 - √3/4] unit²

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: The diameter of the driving wheel of a cart is 154 cm. Calculate the revolution per minute [RPM] of the wheel (approx) in order to keep a speed of 33 Kilo meter per hour.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Diameter of the wheel = 154 cm

Radius of the wheel = 154/2 = 77 cm

Speed = 33km/h

**Formula used:**

Circumference of a circle = 2πr

where r → radius of a circle

Distance covered = speed × time

**Calculation:**

Distance covered in one revolution = Circumference of wheel

⇒ 2πr = 2 × 22/7 × 77 = 484 cm

Speed = 33 km/hr = 33 × 100000/60 = 55000 cm/min

∴ Total Revolutions covered in one min

⇒ 55000/484 = 113.63 ≈ 114

questions.question: Find the radius of the circle x² + y² - 4x + 6y = 12.
questions.solution:
**Formula used:**

General form x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0

Radius r²=g²+f²-c

**Calculation:**

Comparing the equations 

g = -2 , f = 3 ,c = -12

Radius=r=sqrt{g²+f²-c}=sqrt{4+9-(-12)}=sqrt{25}=5

**The radius of the circle is 5 cm**

questions.question: One-quarter of a circular pizza of diameter 28 cm was removed from the whole pizza. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the remaining pizza? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Diameter of pizza = 28cm

**Formula:**

Circumference of circle = πd

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9d241ad8d85bf1cb7894a2c3ffa30413b0031547d40f2ef0b9b0fe6cf9ca8af3.png] 

Radius of pizza = 28/2 = 14cm

Total circumference of pizza = 22/7 × 28 = 88cm

Circumference of 3/4 of pizza = 88 × 3/4 = 66cm

**∴ Perimeter of remaining pizza = 66 + 14 + 14 = 94cm**

questions.question:
In the given figure, O is the centre of the circle, AE is the diameter and ∠AOC = 100°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/99f99023172ee92bc77f1f2905b02b26216ffb55f898005a86bd1c4ca7267202.png] 

The value of ∠CDE + ∠CEA is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

O is the center of the circle.

AE is the diameter.

∠AOC = 100°

**Formula used:**

1. The angle subtended by a chord at the center is twice the angle subtended by the same chord at the circumference.

2. The sum of opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/480e6ad51a6f2817db5570c8a866fed3a5d6656ddb6a9543bc4c3e04bfff91c5.png] 

For ∠CDE:

Consider chord CE

∠COE is the angle subtended by the chord CE at centre and ∠CDE is the angle subtended by the same chord at the circumference.

So, ∠CDE = 1/2 × ∠COE = 1/2 × 80 = 40° 

For ∠CEA:

Consider chord AC

∠AOC is the angle subtended by the chord AC at centre and ∠CEA is the angle subtended by the same chord at the circumference.

So, ∠CEA = 1/2 × ∠AOC = 1/2 × 100 = 50° 

Thus, ∠CDE + ∠CEA = 40 + 50 = 90° 

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**
